fieldNotes.truckGate: Main truck entrance is mid-west side off Commerce Pkwy E Dr. Street View shows a wide paved curb-cut with yellow bollards opening directly onto the truck yard — no barrier arm and no swing/sliding gate across the truck lane. Open driveway = truckGate false.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed booth at or beside the truck entrance in any Street View pass; uncontrolled open driveway.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: False — no truck gate, so no remote check-in implied.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large paved yard between the entrance and the dock faces gives ample internal holding room.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Dense dock-door banks with trailers backed in along the west, east, and north faces — well over 50 doors total (estimate ~95).
fieldNotes.dropArea: Long rows of unhitched trailers in drop position on west, east, and north yards — 50+ band.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Inside the Indianapolis metro fabric (Greenwood) — industrial park abutting a dense residential subdivision to the east; Urban.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Dedicated trailer-storage rows separate from active dock staging on all three truck faces.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale / weigh pad visible in the truck path.
fieldNotes.railServed: No rail spur enters the property.

citations.claim: UNFI's FY2025 Form 10-K, Item 2 Properties, lists a distribution centre at "Greenwood, Indiana" as of 2025-08-02. Our roster address for this record is "655 Commerce Pkwy E Dr, Greenwood, IN 46143".

divestitureCheck.method: Checked against UNFI's FY2025 10-K property table and against its publicly announced 2025-2026 network consolidation. UNFI has closed 12 distribution centres in six years, so presence on the 10-K list alone is not treated as proof of current operation; the announced closures were checked by name.
divestitureCheck.result: present on the FY2025 property list and not named in any announced closure

sources.covers: UNFI network optimisation, the Allentown PA closure, and Central-region consolidations

verification.claimScope: CITY-LEVEL identity only. The 10-K names the city, not the parcel. This record is `probable` rather than `confirmed` because no retrieved source ties UNFI to the specific parcel traced here.
verification.rationale: PROBABLE: UNFI's own SEC 10-K property table lists a distribution centre in Greenwood, Indiana as of 2025-08-02, and this record sits in that city. That establishes the company operates a DC there. It does NOT establish that the parcel traced here is that DC, and no source retrieved in this pass closes that gap, so the verdict stops at probable.
